newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs higher, boosted by rise in U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: JGBs higher, boosted by rise in U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract was higher in early morning trade on Wednesday due to a rise in U.S. Treasuries overnight.
"The rise in U.S. Treasuries caused JGBs to jump above 125.30 at the open, and stop-loss buying is now taking place," said a trader for a trust bank's securities unit.
Cash bonds were also firm due to short-covering by dealers and delta hedging by option dealers, the trader said.
The September stood at 125.38 as of 0048 GMT, up from Tuesday's close of 125.13.
The 190th to 197th 10-year JGBs were firm in particular, due to delta hedging, as they have been commonly used recently as the underlying cash issues in JGB options trading, the trader said.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.250 percent as of 0050 GMT, down from Tuesday's close of 2.275 percent.
The Finance Ministry said it was offering one trillion yen worth of 2.5 percent 10-year JGBs through a price competitive auction on Wednesday.
If the auction attracts over-par bids, it may curb investor demand for the bonds, traders said.

"Judging from this morning's market conditions, the new 10-year JGB issue may be bid at slightly over par, which would make it difficult for investors to buy with enthusiasm," the trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
Even if sales to investors are sluggish initially, however, the market will probably be supported by investors' bargain-hunting needs on the downside, traders said.

Although JGBs may fall in the afternoon due to concern about sluggish investor demand for the new bonds, such a decline is likely to be short-lived, the trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
